findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public with no ACL restricting access, meaning it is likely readable/writable by anyone on the internet, exposing the customer-master.xlsx object stored there.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including sensitive customer data) are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of sensitive data cannot be recovered, compounding the impact of the public exposure.

A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer information to unauthenticated access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled for the financials bucket, increasing risk of unrecoverable data loss or tampering.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so stored operational data is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so stored data science data is not encrypted at rest.
